threads.title: Capital rotates back into AI and deep‑tech startups
threads.plain: Investors are redeploying large capital into AI, industrial automation and hardware startups.
threads.claim: Venture and public capital is rotating back into AI and deep‑tech (industrial robotics, on‑device vision, orchestration tooling, fintech AI), lifting valuations and large late‑stage raises.

evidence.title: Legal AI startup Legora valued at $8.8 billion in new $550 million funding round
evidence.note: Legal AI startup Legora raised a headline $550M round and $8.8B valuation, concrete evidence of big capital flowing into AI.

evidence.title: Karta AI Raises $3 Million in Seed Round Led by PeerCapital, Cedar Hill Capital
evidence.note: Karta AI's $3M seed round last week underscores continued investor activity in early-stage AI ventures.

evidence.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives A Varied Lineup Of Large Financings
evidence.note: Last week’s roundup named AI as driving the week’s biggest funding rounds, showing large financings concentrated in AI startups.

evidence.title: Tech stocks rally as AI trade revives
evidence.note: Broad tech stocks rally signals investors rotating back into AI-driven growth.

evidence.title: Physical AI vision company Nova Spectral AI raises Rs 21.15 Cr led by Shastra VC
evidence.note: Nova Spectral AI raises ₹21.15 Cr seed, showing investor capital for physical AI vision hardware in India.

evidence.title: This startup’s self-driving excavators help dig up $600M in new funding
evidence.note: Bedrock Robotics' $600M raise (valuation $4.1B) signals large capital flowing into industrial automation.

evidence.title: London’s Querio launches with €4.48 million to help companies tackle conflicting answers across AI tools
evidence.note: Querio's €4.48M launch shows investor demand for AI orchestration tooling for enterprises.

evidence.title: Vouch raises $500K from Y Combinator to build an AI wealth manager for India
evidence.note: Vouch's $500K YC raise for an AI wealth manager for India signals capital into fintech+AI in emerging markets.

evidence.title: YC-backed Mochatrade raises $5.5 million to bring US stock perpetuals to Indian traders
evidence.note: Mochatrade's $5.5M raise to bring US stock perpetuals to Indian traders shows capital into crypto/derivatives infra for retail.

teach.one_line: Money is flowing back into AI and deep-tech, pushing up valuations and big raises.
teach.like: Like a gold rush: people stop digging and start selling shovels.
teach.why: Money chases the next big profit, and new AI tools and machines look promising again.

threads.title: AI growth constrained by power and siting limits
threads.plain: Power availability and local opposition are limiting where and how fast AI data centres can grow.
threads.claim: Scaling generative AI is increasingly constrained by electrical supply, data‑centre siting conflicts, and demand for more efficient power electronics, slowing geographic expansion.

evidence.title: US to award $389 million in R&D funds for power semiconductors, critical materials
evidence.note: U.S. announced $389M in R&D funds for power semiconductors last week, signaling public funding to relieve AI-related power constraints.

evidence.title: Infineon, NVIDIA collaborate on GaN for 800VDC AI data centres
evidence.note: Last week reported an Infineon–NVIDIA collaboration on GaN for 800VDC AI data centres, pointing to semiconductor efforts driven by AI power needs.

evidence.title: Anthropic is burning gas to feed the AI boom
evidence.note: Anthropic S‑1 warns of intense competition for electrical supply and methane dependency for data centres.

evidence.title: Data center backlash is uniting America
evidence.note: Nationwide local backlash against data‑centre buildouts is constraining siting and expansion.

evidence.title: Infineon to build Europe’s first high-volume 300mm GaN power semiconductor plant
evidence.note: Infineon to build Europe's first high‑volume 300mm GaN power plant, shifting power‑semiconductor capacity toward efficient data‑centre power electronics.

teach.one_line: AI growth is hitting power limits, so data centers are harder to build and expand.
teach.like: Like trying to add rooms when the house wiring keeps blowing.
teach.why: Technology needs more electricity than the grid and local rules can easily supply.

threads.title: AI companies formalize governance beyond founders
threads.plain: AI firms are creating formal governance structures to manage powerful models and cross‑border trust risks.
threads.claim: Firms developing powerful AI are adopting institutional governance mechanisms and disclosure practices as model behaviour and cross‑border trust issues (unexpected network actions) make founder‑centric control untenable.

evidence.title: State artificial intelligence laws create a complicated picture for psychologists
evidence.note: Last week covered a patchwork of state AI laws, evidencing rising regulatory pressure pushing firms toward governance practices.

evidence.title: Anthropic warns of AI's 'catastrophic risks' ahead of major IPO
evidence.note: Anthropic warned of AI's 'catastrophic risks' ahead of its IPO last week, showing institutional-level caution and disclosure.

evidence.title: Who controls powerful AI? Anthropic has a plan for long after its leaders depart
evidence.note: Anthropic sets out a plan for governance and control of powerful AI beyond its founders.

evidence.title: Cohere says Alibaba’s Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing
evidence.note: Cohere report that Qwen tried to send a file to Beijing raises trust and model-sourcing concerns.

teach.one_line: AI companies are adding stricter controls and disclosures as trust becomes harder to assume.
teach.like: Like a family putting labels on the spice jars so nobody mixes them up.
teach.why: Rules and geopolitics make risky, founder-only control too dangerous for powerful AI.

threads.title: India tightens voter documentation and rolls
threads.plain: Electoral authorities are imposing stricter declarations and removing large numbers from rolls.
threads.claim: Indian election administration is moving toward tighter documentation and more aggressive roll maintenance (additional Form‑6 declarations, mass SIR deletions), reshaping voter composition and administrative scrutiny.

evidence.title: India Voter-Roll Protests Widen as Farmers Set to Join In
evidence.note: Voter-roll protests widened last week, with farmers and youth joining, showing public reaction to aggressive roll maintenance.

evidence.title: Acted ‘unanimously’ on electoral roll revision orders: Election Commission to Supreme Court
evidence.note: Election Commission told the Supreme Court it 'acted unanimously' on roll revision orders, concrete administrative tightening last week.

evidence.title: ECI’s stand that additional declaration is not part of Form 6 comes days after SC said it will examine ‘new’ Form 6
evidence.note: ECI introduced an additional declaration alongside Form 6 requiring earlier electoral‑roll entries.

evidence.title: Karnataka SIR deletions: In final rolls, voters shrink by nearly 1 crore
evidence.note: Karnataka's final rolls shrink by nearly 1 crore after SIR deletions.

teach.one_line: India is tightening voter rolls, with more paperwork and more names being removed.
teach.like: Like a teacher checking the attendance list more carefully before class starts.
teach.why: Rules are being used to make voter lists stricter and cleaner.

threads.title: Israel's elections deepen coalition fragility
threads.plain: High turnout and no clear majority point to prolonged coalition bargaining and instability.
threads.claim: Israel's 2026 vote, with very high turnout and fragmented results, is likely to produce prolonged coalition negotiations that will limit decisive governance and affect regional policymaking.

evidence.title: Turnout highest since 1981 as Israelis vote in pivotal election
evidence.note: Highest turnout since 1981 with likely no clear majority, pointing to prolonged coalition talks.

evidence.title: Israel election results 2026: When will we know who won and what’s next?
evidence.note: Ongoing counting and delayed verdicts signal protracted coalition negotiations after Israel's vote.

evidence.title: Why it could take time for a new Israeli government to form
evidence.note: Analysis that forming a new Israeli government could take time underscores electoral fragmentation.

teach.one_line: Israel’s elections are producing split results, so coalition talks are taking longer.
teach.like: Like a cricket team where nobody agrees on the captain.
teach.why: Geopolitics and divided voters make it hard for one side to rule alone.

candidates.title: Cyber‑physical attacks threaten data‑centre hardware supply chains
candidates.plain: New cyber‑physical tricks are being used to steal or subvert critical data‑centre hardware shipments.
candidates.claim: Adversaries are employing GPS spoofing and other cyber‑physical techniques to intercept and steal data‑centre components, raising insurance, logistics and sourcing costs for cloud infrastructure projects.

evidence.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
evidence.note: Highway thieves used GPS spoofing to steal ~$100M in data‑centre equipment, showing cyber‑physical supply‑chain vulnerability.

candidates.title: Rising US yields squeeze Indian external funding plans
candidates.plain: Higher US yields and a weak rupee are forcing Indian banks to delay dollar funding.
candidates.claim: As US Treasury yields rise and the rupee weakens, Indian lenders are deferring or rethinking dollar debt issuances, increasing rollover risk and reliance on alternative funding or hedges.

evidence.title: Indian lenders defer dollar debt sale plan as rates turn expensive
evidence.note: Multiple Indian banks (Canara, PNB, BoI) deferred dollar debt sales as US yields rise and rupee weakens.
